answer.answer: PVE34 remains valid historical evidence for a safe fixed Nyx profile, but it no longer defines the operating model. Later results established an evidence-driven, reversible controller whose settings vary by source and pressure shape. The next safe step is a bounded alpha soak with full integrity gates and crash-restart proof before any unattended run.

claims.value: The historical 10M crossing run `split-lanes-64f-pve34-pvp2-other1-200k-to10m-20260523T115711Z` inserted `210624` rows, finished at `10.019M`, and crossed `10,000,000` at elapsed `442s`. Its steady average over elapsed `220-490s` was about `403/sec`, late pre-stop average about `408/sec`, and drain average about `372/sec`, with `0` parser errors, retries, duplicates, or terminal markers. Summary recomputation for `1-10019225`, sampled membership, final-chunk S3 and coverage checks, and protected D2 Redis counts all passed. It established PVE34 as the best practical fixed Nyx profile in that data band and showed that the write path—not fetching—was limiting throughput; it did not establish PVE34 as a universal setting.

Later evidence superseded the fixed-profile operating model without invalidating PVE34’s historical result. The durable model treats fetch workers, batches, fixed-budget DB-lane allocation, and rollup workers as measured optimization controls: autoscaler state is never correctness state; accepted settings must remain reversible and scenario-specific. Current-code alpha reached `1083.1 PGCR/sec` average and `1201.8/sec` final/max; a corrected alpha run reduced fetch to `32`, rolled back, and raised it again on demonstrated underfeed. Beta with sustained `760ms` artificial latency correctly scaled fetch to `128` without adding DB workers; delta slow-edge operation reduced fetch/retry workers to floor `4`; gamma parser-owned S3 reached `2141.3/sec` average, `2243.0/sec` steady, and `2469.0/sec` final/max, making DB-lane tuning useful there. Consequently, `112` has no source-level seed, target, or floor semantics; batch `128` is a learned keeper-family ceiling rather than a law; and gamma’s successful `35/6 -> 36/5` rebalance is not an alpha default. The later final scorecard recorded D1 PASS for alpha, beta, gamma, delta, epsilon, zeta, eta, and theta, while Stage 3 D1 full replay, full S3 verification, and restart proof remained not run.

claims.value: Integrity remains non-negotiable: DB rows are truth; raw-marker commits travel atomically with summaries; protected D2 Redis namespaces remain read-only; autoscaler state cannot become correctness state; Cortex cannot enter the parser DB-write path; and parser-owned S3 reads stay in the parser fetch path. Every bounded run must retain contiguous raw coverage by count, `raw_failed_pgcrs=0`, S3 ledger/readback verification, a cache tail containing only the normal partial batch, Datadog visibility, healthy host Redis, bounded MySQL/host memory and CPU pressure, and no parser/Cortex process left running. Stop/drain is part of the autonomy contract: uncommitted in-memory work may be discarded, but DB queues owning fetched PGCRs drain, and the next ordinary parser run fills the tail from durable DB truth. Recovery must never depend on rebuild/recompute, a parser-state correctness table, Cortex S3 replay, special gap-fill, manual row repair, or unsafe deletion of sparse repair evidence. Before unattended operation, TERM/KILL recovery must prove resume from durable DB/Redis truth; the later D2 repair evidence further requires cursor movement to succeed before dependent repair rows are deleted and cache-position proof failures to retry rather than become PGCR parse failures.

claims.value: The next safe experiment is a bounded longer alpha soak using learned priors, the current batch ceiling `128`, measured fetch control, and one-worker-at-a-time fixed-budget DB rebalance with accept-or-rollback and host CPU/MySQL memory pressure included in the decision loop. It must run with D1 Cortex/S3 companion coverage and enforce contiguous raw coverage, `raw_failed_pgcrs=0`, verified S3 ledger/readback, a normal partial cache tail only, protected D2 Redis stability, Datadog/host-health visibility, and final process hygiene. Before extending this to any unattended long run, add TERM/KILL restart evidence showing recovery without manual repair from durable DB/Redis truth. Gamma should remain a separate parser-owned-S3 DB-lane experiment with enough queue capacity for controller observations; its `36/5` behavior must not be generalized to alpha. Active rollup-worker autotuning and durable controller persistence remain deferred until in-process behavior is calm and simple.

answer.answer: Revised the mega-base into a capacity-safe, distributed Update 1 factory plan and persisted checkpoint `checkpoint:b539da12-728b-f5e2-fe6d-1a4e762f248e`. The architecture and operating choices are proposals; the 1,000-capacity limit and cited building/logistics specifications are established facts.

claims.value: Replace the monolithic mega-base with a protected core campus plus distributed extraction and processing outposts connected by powered rail trunks. The current level-0 Base Core has 1,000 capacity, and exceeding it disables Fire Wave protection, so retain explicit headroom below 1,000. Defer or separately budget heavy production: a Constructorizer uses 500 capacity and a Facturer 650, exceeding the entire level-0 budget together. Use only Update 1 content; Rail v.4/v.5 and hidden or future-facing buildings are excluded.

Use one item per line where practical and match live rail capacity to source flow: Rail v.1 for 120 items/min, v.2 for 240 items/min, and v.3 for up to 480 items/min. Upgrade only aggregate trunks whose summed flow requires it; rails also distribute power. Place a 400-item Storage Depot v.1 or 1,600-item Storage Depot v.2 between production and consumption as the working buffer. If Clever L12 is unlocked, use the 2,500-capacity multi-item Multistorage only as end-of-line overflow. The intended operating transition is producer → item-specific working buffer → consumer/exporter, with overflow preventing upstream backup.

For exports, dedicate one Orbital Cargo Launcher to each chosen export product because every launcher has one input, and feed each launcher from its own product buffer so reputation flow does not starve; actual export SKUs and sustained rates remain to be selected from this save’s live unlocks. For defense, provide at least one Defense Tower t2 position supplied from the ammo printer by a thin Rail v.1 spur or loop; Defense Turret t1 is manual-feed only and is not the automated-defense assumption.

Test next in game: (1) which corporation export products are currently unlocked and each launcher’s sustained consumption rate; (2) whether Rail Modulator merges use round-robin or priority under saturation; (3) whether Multirail lanes have independent throughput; (4) the effective Drone Station coverage radius; (5) whether Delivery Storage exists in Update 1; (6) whether Base Core Amplifier v.1/v.2 add the described 50/20 capacity or correspond to the conflicting −250/−20 temperature fields; (7) whether the listed Base Core upgrade item mix is correct in the current build; and (8) ammo consumption during a representative attack, including whether one buffered Rail v.1 spur keeps the Defense Tower t2 supplied and recovers after drawdown.

checkpoint.objective: Revise the earlier Star Rupture mega-base idea for a save currently limited to Base Core level 0 and Early Access Update 1.
current_state: Verified Base Core level 0 capacity is 1,000 and protection fails if capacity is exceeded.
Verified live logistics tiers are Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 at 120/240/480 items/min.
The revised architecture is a proposal and has not yet been verified as built in the save.
decisions: Use a protected core campus with distributed extraction and processing outposts.
Keep explicit capacity headroom and defer the combined Constructorizer/Facturer load.
Use tier-matched, mostly single-item rail lines with 400- or 1,600-item working buffers.
Use one buffered launcher per export product.
Provide a Rail v.1-fed Defense Tower t2 ammo spur.
open_questions: Current export unlocks and launcher consumption rates.
Rail Modulator queue policy and Multirail lane independence.
Drone Station coverage and Delivery Storage availability.
Actual amplifier capacity effects and Base Core upgrade item mix.
Defense ammo drawdown and recovery behavior.
next_actions: Inventory current unlocks, placed loads, and remaining capacity.
Run saturated merge and Multirail tests.
Measure Drone Station coverage and inspect Delivery Storage availability.
Select current export targets and measure launcher drain.
Run a representative defended attack and record ammo-buffer behavior.
